description: External Solid-OIDC + UMA 2.0 deployments (Solid-OIDC §9, SolidUmaTokenProvider). Live, configured wholly by environment; missing configuration is UNTESTED. No mock UMA server is listed here: the repository's test/helpers/uma.js is a unit-test fixture, not interoperability evidence.

targets.name: Inrupt PodSpaces storage via its UMA authorization server (Solid-OIDC §9 ID token claim push)

software.name: Inrupt Enterprise Solid Server (PodSpaces), UMA service

notes: public discovery 2026-09-27 (unauthenticated GETs only): https://storage.inrupt.com/<path> answered 401 with WWW-Authenticate: UMA as_uri="https://uma.inrupt.com", ticket="…", then Bearer and DPoP challenges; https://uma.inrupt.com/.well-known/uma2-configuration has issuer https://uma.inrupt.com, token_endpoint https://uma.inrupt.com/token, grant_types_supported [uma-ticket] and uma_profiles_supported including http://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDToken (and a VC profile)
the UMA server is on another origin than the storage, so it is trusted explicitly (umaServers); the Solid-OIDC issuer is https://login.inrupt.com
whether PodSpaces issues an RPT for a pushed login.inrupt.com ID token (and whether that ID token carries cnf) has not been observed: no test account was used
unattended (session mode): unverified — login.inrupt.com may show a consent page for a newly registered client; the non-interactive login fails closed if it does

Solid UMA evidence requires the whole Solid-OIDC §9 flow on the wire (UMA challenge with as_uri and ticket, uma2-configuration advertising the ID token profile, uma-ticket grant pushing the DPoP-bound ID token, RPT use); an ordinary OAuth Bearer or DPoP access token — e.g. from Keycloak — never counts
claims gathering (need_info with redirect_user) is not automated by the library: a deployment that asks for more claims FAILs uma.login-read with that reason

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_WEBID
env.description: WebID of a dedicated test account on Inrupt PodSpaces; its profile names the Solid-OIDC issuer

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_STORAGE
env.description: storage of the test account (ends with /); the credential boundary

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_SCRATCH
env.description: container dedicated to test writes inside the storage (ends with /); omit for read-only runs

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_PRIVATE_RESOURCE
env.description: an existing private resource of the test account whose unauthenticated GET answers 401 with an UMA challenge (read-only runs)

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_OTHER_PROTECTED
env.description: a protected resource outside the test storage (read-only boundary probe)

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_ISSUER
env.description: the Solid-OIDC issuer expected in the ID token (override; defaults to the observed one)

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_UMA_SERVER
env.description: the UMA authorization server (as_uri) to trust (override; defaults to the observed one)

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_CLIENT_ID
env.description: optional Solid-OIDC Client Identifier Document URL (its redirect_uris must include the redirect URI); omit to use dynamic registration

env.name: RA_INTEROP_INRUPT_PODSPACES_UMA_STORAGE_STATE
env.description: Playwright storageState file of a dedicated test account's signed-in identity-provider session (contains cookies; never commit). With --headed it seeds the browser; without --headed it enables the fail-closed non-interactive session mode (a configured file that does not exist is a configuration error)

env.name: RA_INTEROP_SOLID_REDIRECT_URI
env.description: loopback redirect URI (default http://127.0.0.1:39398/callback); with a Client Identifier Document it must be one of the document's redirect_uris

capabilityNotes.writes: whether an RPT obtained with the ID token claim authorizes a create-only PUT (201) and conditional updates in the scratch container has not been observed (no test account yet)

targets.name: Configured Solid-OIDC + UMA deployment (any resource server answering UMA challenges with a Solid-OIDC-profile UMA server)
notes: configure a deployment you are allowed to test (e.g. a self-hosted ESS, or a Solid server fronted by a Solid-OIDC-profile UMA server); the UMA server's uma2-configuration must list the ID token profile in uma_profiles_supported
unattended (session mode): depends on the Solid-OIDC provider's session, consent and MFA policies; unverified

Solid UMA evidence requires the whole Solid-OIDC §9 flow on the wire (UMA challenge with as_uri and ticket, uma2-configuration advertising the ID token profile, uma-ticket grant pushing the DPoP-bound ID token, RPT use); an ordinary OAuth Bearer or DPoP access token — e.g. from Keycloak — never counts
claims gathering (need_info with redirect_user) is not automated by the library: a deployment that asks for more claims FAILs uma.login-read with that reason
